analogs.covers: Almost everything: a lone, water-loving apex cat that marks favourite trees and takes the biggest prey

headline: A lone jaguar the size of a tiger: water-loving, tree-marking, and ready to fight any other apex for the right to stay.

setting.label: Nomad of canyons, coasts and forest edges
setting.note: Nomadic, lingering in a few preferred areas where rivals are rarer. Loves bathing in small ponds and napping in the shade.

playsLike: You are an Apex daytime hunter who thrives alone. Bonds are fragile: brothers, a mother and her kits, or a pair that only becomes lifelong after 5 successful nests. You may hunt any tier, Apex herbivores first, but you must first challenge any Tyrannosaurus, Tyrannotitan or other Giganotosaurus in the POI, or leave. Alone you leave the giant sauropods alone and only take them on with a temporary partner.

why.text: 'Thrive in solitude', avoids others of its kind and forms temporary bonds that split again when the opportunity has passed (official inspiration: jaguars, leopards, black panthers).
Enjoys water, bathes in small ponds and naps in shade. Jaguars are the water-loving big cats.
Rubs its cheeks on favourite trees, rocks and landmarks to mark them, exactly as big cats do.
Must challenge Tyrannosaurus, Tyrannotitan and other Giganotosaurus before hunting, or leave. A big cat will not share its hunting ground with another top predator.
Apex tier, 5,500 combat weight, 1,000 HP, sprint 850 held for 50 s.

notLike: Jaguars are night-leaning ambushers; Giganotosaurus hunts by day and is described as an endurance hunter that runs prey down.
Jaguars hunt alone; a solo Giganotosaurus teams up temporarily to take giant sauropods.
twist: Think one of the biggest, boldest cats on the map; peregrine falcons are also named as inspiration for its drive.
